goals.name: 35% to 56% reduction in sediment loading
goals.description: The sediment/siltation TMDL for Moon Lake calls for a 35% to 56% cut in sediment loading to waterbodies in the Yazoo Pass watershed. This is the plan's expected load reduction target.
goals.targetText: 35% to 56% reduction in the sediment loading
goals.sourceQuote: The TMDL for sedimentation/siltation on Moon Lake called for a 35% to 56% reduction in the sediment loading to the waterbodies within the watershed.

goals.name: Eliminate all open pipes and inadequate wastewater treatment systems
goals.description: To reduce fecal coliform loading to Moon Lake, the Phase One fecal coliform TMDL recommends eliminating all direct pipes and inadequate individual septic systems.
goals.targetText: elimination of all open pipes and inadequate individual wastewater treatment systems
goals.sourceQuote: MDEQ recommended that a reduction in the observed potential pollutant load be achieved through the elimination of all open pipes and inadequate individual wastewater treatment systems.

goals.name: Meet E. coli pathogen criterion
goals.description: Lake waters must meet the state E. coli criterion for pathogens. The plan uses this criterion to judge whether load reductions are achieved.
goals.targetText: 30-day geometric mean of 126 per 100 ml; not exceed 410 per 100 ml more than 10% of the time
goals.sourceQuote: For pathogens, waters must meet a 30-day geometric mean of 126 per 100 ml, nor should the samples examined during the 30-day period exceed 410 per 100 ml more than 10% of the time for E. coli.

goals.name: Behavior change and BMP use to improve water quality
goals.description: The information and education program aims to change behavior and increase adoption of BMPs. The intended outcome is improved water quality and quality of life in the watershed.
goals.targetText: improve water quality and the overall quality of life in the watershed
goals.sourceQuote: The ultimate goal is to bring about behavior changes and the use of “best management practices” that will improve water quality and the overall quality of life in the watershed.

bmps.name: Grade Stabilization Structure
bmps.description: Grade stabilization structures proposed for full-scale restoration of the watershed to control gully erosion and sediment loss. An initial Phase 1 would install 5 of them for $32,400.
bmps.sectionTitle: Element d: Technical and Financial Assistance

bmps.name: Water Control Structure
bmps.description: Water control structures, both slotted and riser pipes, proposed to address gully erosion in the watershed. Phase 1 would install 40 of them for $96,000.
bmps.sectionTitle: Element d: Technical and Financial Assistance

bmps.name: Vegetated Ditch
bmps.description: Two-stage vegetated ditches proposed as a structural measure to reduce sheet and rill erosion and sediment delivery.
bmps.sectionTitle: Element d: Technical and Financial Assistance

bmps.name: Cover Crop
bmps.description: Cover crops proposed on cropland to address sheet and rill erosion and nutrient loss, with technical and financial assistance from Delta F.A.R.M. Phase 1 covers three 80-acre sites over 2 years for $35,040.
bmps.sectionTitle: Element d: Technical and Financial Assistance

bmps.name: Nutrient Management
bmps.description: Nutrient management is listed among the BMPs Delta F.A.R.M. identified to mitigate sediment issues in the watershed. No quantity or cost is given.
bmps.sourceQuote: Water Control Structure Vegetated Ditches Grade Stabilization Structures Cover Crops Nutrient Management

bmps.name: Low-grade weirs
bmps.description: Low-grade weirs are named as a structural measure to address sheet and rill erosion in the ridge and swale topography of the watershed.
bmps.sourceQuote: Structural measures include low-grade weirs and two-stage vegetated ditches.

bmps.name: Reduced tillage
bmps.description: Reduced tillage is a non-structural soil health practice that Delta F.A.R.M. will work with farmers to implement in priority areas prone to high sediment and nutrient loss.
bmps.location: priority areas prone to high rates of sediment and nutrient loss
bmps.sourceQuote: Non-structural practices such as cover crops and reduced tillage are proven to be the best method of addressing sheet and rill erosion.

bmps.name: Septic system maintenance support
bmps.description: MDEQ will work with lakeside landowners to identify funding sources for septic system maintenance needs, to address pathogen inputs to Moon Lake.
bmps.sourceQuote: Where possible, MDEQ will work with landowners to identify potential funding sources to support any maintenance needs.

implementation.name: Develop and execute Sub-Grant Agreement
implementation.description: Once the 9 Key Element plan is approved, the grantee and MDEQ develop and execute a sub-grant agreement that sets out the grantee's roles, tasks, requirements and milestones.
implementation.sourceQuote: Upon approval of 9 Key Element Watershed Plan, the grantee shall work with MDEQ to develop, execute, and implement a Sub-Grant Agreement that defines the roles, tasks, requirements, and milestones of the grantee. (Month 1)

implementation.name: Determine priority areas contributing significant pollutant loading
implementation.description: The grantee, with MDEQ, identifies the priority areas that contribute significant pollutant loads so implementation can be targeted.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee, with assistance from MDEQ, shall determine priority areas that are contributing significant pollutant loading to the watershed. (Months 1-2)

implementation.name: Identify members and develop Watershed Implementation Team (WIT)
implementation.description: The grantee helps identify members for, and form, the Watershed Implementation Team that will guide the project.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee, with assistance from MDEQ, shall assist in the identification of members and development of a Watershed Implementation Team (WIT). (Months 1-2)

implementation.name: Develop Watershed Based Plan (WBP)
implementation.description: The grantee and the WIT develop a Watershed Based Plan with tasks to reduce sediment and pathogen loadings. The 9 Key Element Plan is attached to it.
implementation.sourceQuote: pathogen loadings to waterbodies within the watershed. This WBP will include the 9 Key Element Plan as an attachment. (Months 24-36)

implementation.name: Assist development and implementation of watershed monitoring plan
implementation.description: The grantee works with the WIT, MDEQ and others to develop and carry out a monitoring plan for the project.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee, in cooperation with the WIT, MDEQ, and others, shall assist in the development and implementation of a watershed monitoring plan for the project (Months 1- 36).

implementation.name: Inform priority-area landowners and secure commitments
implementation.description: The grantee informs landowners and operators in priority areas about the project and secures commitments from those willing to take part.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee shall inform landowners and operators within the identified priority areas about the project and secure commitments from these priority-area landowners and operators who are willing to participate in the project. (Months 1-12)

implementation.name: Develop plans for BMP installation on priority lands
implementation.description: The grantee prepares installation plans for BMPs on priority lands, consistent with the approved WBP.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee, in accordance with the previously submitted and approved WBP, shall develop plans for the installation of BMPs on priority lands within the watershed. (Months 2-36)

implementation.name: Assist participants in installing approved BMPs
implementation.description: The grantee helps participants install approved BMPs following the NRCS Technical Field Manual or other approved guidelines.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee shall assist participants in installing approved BMPs. All BMPs shall be installed in accordance with the guidelines developed in the latest edition of the NRCS Technical Field Manual, or other approved guidelines. (Months 2-36)

implementation.name: Notify MDEQ project officer of site locations, inspections and meetings
implementation.description: The grantee gives the MDEQ project officer timely notice of project sites, inspections and public meetings so the officer can attend.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee shall, in a timely manner, notify MDEQ project officer of all project-site locations/inspections/public meetings so that MDEQ project officer may have the opportunity to attend. (Months 2-36)

implementation.name: Collect GPS coordinates of implemented practices in GIS format
implementation.description: The grantee records GPS locations of all implemented practices and puts them into GIS, following Federal Geographic Data Committee standards.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee shall collect relevant GPS coordinates of all implemented practices and incorporate into GIS format. All geospatial data shall be collected in a manner consistent with the Federal Geographic Data Committee endorsed standards. (Months 1-36)

implementation.name: Photo documentation of implemented practices
implementation.description: The grantee photographs each practice before, during and after installation.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee shall take adequate photo documentation before, during, and after the installation of the implemented practice. (Months 1-36)

implementation.name: Submit quarterly reports
implementation.description: The grantee submits quarterly progress reports by the 25th of April, July, October and January, showing task status and start and completion dates.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee shall submit quarterly reports not later than the 25th of April, July, October, and January of each year showing the status of tasks and start/completion dates of each task. (Months 1-36)

implementation.name: Make project presentations as requested by MDEQ
implementation.description: The grantee gives presentations on the project when MDEQ requests them.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee shall make project presentations as requested by MDEQ. (Month 1-36)

implementation.name: Assist MDEQ project officer with construction inspections
implementation.description: The grantee helps the MDEQ project officer carry out inspections while BMPs are being built.
implementation.sourceQuote: The grantee shall assist the MDEQ project officer in conducting inspections during construction. (Months 3-36)

implementation.name: Submit final report to MDEQ
implementation.description: The grantee submits a final report covering pollutant reductions or water quality improvements, acreage affected, pre- and post-site conditions and GIS data, and revises it if MDEQ asks.
implementation.sourceQuote: shall submit a final report to MDEQ to include measured, or estimated, nonpoint source pollutant reductions or water quality improvements, acreage affected, preand post- site conditions, and GIS data. The grantee shall make revisions, if necessary, upon the request of MDEQ. (Month 36)

implementation.name: Coordinate with MDEQ, NRCS, USGS and partners to target priority areas
implementation.description: Milestone to coordinate with agencies and partners on priority BMP areas contributing significant pollutant loads to Moon Lake.
implementation.sourceQuote: Coordinate with the MDEQ, NRCS, | Target priority areas | Month 1-6

implementation.name: Establish Watershed Implementation Team
implementation.description: Milestone to set up the WIT, which then begins refining the Watershed Based Plan.
implementation.sourceQuote: Establish Watershed Implementation | Establish WIT | Month 1-2

implementation.name: Initiate watershed monitoring
implementation.description: Milestone to start baseline condition monitoring.
implementation.sourceQuote: Initiate watershed monitoring | Baseline condition monitoring | Month 3-12

implementation.name: Meet with landowners and cooperators to secure BMP commitments
implementation.description: Milestone to obtain landowner commitments to install BMPs in priority areas.
implementation.sourceQuote: Meet with landowners and cooperators | Landowner | Months 1-6

implementation.name: Establish routine WIT meeting schedule
implementation.description: Milestone to hold regular WIT meetings that support WBP implementation and revision.
implementation.sourceQuote: Establish routine meeting schedule for WIT to support WBP implementation/ revision | WIT meetings | Months 1-36

implementation.name: Implement BMPs
implementation.description: Milestone for installing BMPs in the watershed.
implementation.sourceQuote: Implement BMPs | BMP installation | Months 12-36

implementation.name: Inspect BMPs installed with Section 319 funds
implementation.description: Milestone to coordinate with Delta F.A.R.M. on inspecting BMPs installed with Section 319 funding.
implementation.sourceQuote: Coordinate with Delta F.A.R.M. to inspect BMPs that were installed using | BMP Inspection | Months 24-36

implementation.name: Begin post-BMP water quality monitoring
implementation.description: Milestone to start collecting water quality data after BMPs are installed.
implementation.sourceQuote: Begin monitoring to collect data on post-BMP water quality | Post-BMP Monitoring | Months 30-42

implementation.name: Finalize education and outreach plan
implementation.description: Milestone to finalize the education and outreach plan, resulting in scheduled outreach events.
implementation.sourceQuote: Finalize education and outreach plan | Education/Outreach events scheduled | Months 8-36

implementation.name: Finalize revised WBP
implementation.description: Milestone to complete the final revised Watershed Based Plan.
implementation.sourceQuote: Finalize revised WBP | Final Revised WBP | Months 28-36

implementation.name: Delta F.A.R.M. implements conservation strategies
implementation.description: Delta F.A.R.M. is named as the partner that will carry out conservation strategies for the Yazoo Pass Watershed under this plan.
implementation.sourceQuote: Under this watershed plan, Delta F.A.R.M. will implement conservation strategies for the Yazoo Pass Watershed.

implementation.name: Identify NRCS program opportunities and assist producers
implementation.description: Delta F.A.R.M. will look for BMP opportunities under NRCS programs and help producers through application and implementation.
implementation.sourceQuote: Delta F.A.R.M. will also identify opportunities for BMP implementation through NRCS covered programs and provide assistance to producers throughout the application and implementation process.

implementation.name: Phase 1 project management, implementation, coordination and plan revision
implementation.description: Budgeted project management, coordination and plan revision costs for the initial implementation phase.
implementation.sourceQuote: Implementation, Coordination, $54,660

implementation.name: Stressor Analysis if no water quality improvement
implementation.description: If end-of-project data show little or no improvement, a Stressor Analysis will be run to find new or additional stressors, and the WIT will then identify follow-up actions.
implementation.sourceQuote: In the event data indicate little or no positive change, a Stressor Analysis will be conducted to determine if any new or additional stressors are preventing improvements to water quality.

monitoring.name: Dissolved Oxygen daily average threshold
monitoring.description: Water quality criterion for dissolved oxygen used to measure compliance: a daily average of at least 5.0 mg/L.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Threshold Daily Average of 5.0 mg/L; Instantaneous threshold of 4.0

monitoring.name: Dissolved Oxygen instantaneous threshold
monitoring.description: Instantaneous dissolved oxygen criterion of 4.0 mg/L used to measure compliance with water quality criteria.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Instantaneous threshold of 4.0

monitoring.name: Temperature threshold
monitoring.description: Water temperature criterion not to exceed 90°F.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Temperature | Not to exceed 90°F

monitoring.name: Specific Conductance threshold
monitoring.description: Specific conductance criterion of less than 1000 micromhos/cm.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Specific Conductance | Less Than 1000 micromhos/cm

monitoring.name: Dissolved Solids monthly average threshold
monitoring.description: Dissolved solids criterion: monthly average less than 750 mg/L.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Monthly average less than 750 mg/L

monitoring.name: Dissolved Solids instantaneous threshold
monitoring.description: Dissolved solids instantaneous criterion of less than 1500 mg/L.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Dissolved Solids | threshold less than 1500 mg/L

monitoring.name: Turbidity threshold
monitoring.description: Turbidity criterion of less than 100 NTU, used as a sediment surrogate.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Turbidity | <100 NTU

monitoring.name: Total Suspended Solids threshold
monitoring.description: Total suspended solids criterion of less than 80 mg/l, used as a sediment surrogate.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Total Suspended Solids | <80 mg/l

monitoring.name: E. coli 30-day geometric mean criterion
monitoring.description: Pathogen criterion requiring a 30-day geometric mean of E. coli no greater than 126 per 100 ml.
monitoring.sourceQuote: For pathogens, waters must meet a 30-day geometric mean of 126 per 100 ml, nor should the samples examined during the 30-day period exceed 410 per 100 ml more than 10% of the time for E. coli.

monitoring.name: E. coli single-sample criterion
monitoring.description: Pathogen criterion: samples during a 30-day period should not exceed 410 per 100 ml more than 10% of the time.
monitoring.frequency: not more than 10% of samples in a 30-day period
monitoring.sourceQuote: For pathogens, waters must meet a 30-day geometric mean of 126 per 100 ml, nor should the samples examined during the 30-day period exceed 410 per 100 ml more than 10% of the time for E. coli.

monitoring.name: Sediment surrogate parameter monitoring
monitoring.description: Because there is no numeric sediment criterion, the monitoring plan will measure surrogates such as total suspended solids, total suspended sediment and turbidity along with conventional parameters.
monitoring.parameter: Total suspended solids, total suspended sediment, turbidity
monitoring.sourceQuote: In lieu of numeric criteria for sediment, the monitoring plan will be designed to collect data on parameters that are considered surrogates for sediment concentrations and may include measurements for total suspended solids, total suspended sediment, and turbidity

monitoring.name: Biological community and in-stream habitat surveys
monitoring.description: Biological community data and in-stream habitat surveys will be collected during the project to identify trends and evaluate whether implementation is improving water quality.
monitoring.frequency: over the course of the project
monitoring.sourceQuote: In addition to chemical data, biological community data and in stream habitat surveys will be collected over the course of the project.

monitoring.name: Edge of field monitoring
monitoring.description: MDEQ and Delta F.A.R.M. will seek opportunities with partners to establish edge of field monitoring.
monitoring.parameter: Edge of field runoff water quality
monitoring.sourceQuote: MDEQ and Delta F.A.R.M. will work with other watershed partners to identify opportunities to establish edge of field monitoring.

monitoring.name: Moon Lake ambient lake monitoring
monitoring.description: MDEQ will continue monitoring Moon Lake under the state's Ambient Lake Monitoring Program.
monitoring.sourceQuote: MDEQ will continue to monitor Moon Lake as part of the state’s Ambient Lake Monitoring Program.

monitoring.name: E. coli monitoring in Moon Lake
monitoring.description: MDEQ will collect E. coli samples in Moon Lake to monitor for pathogens linked to septic systems and direct pipes.
monitoring.sourceQuote: In addition to ambient monitoring, MDEQ will collect E. coli in the lake to monitor for pathogens.

monitoring.name: Pre-implementation baseline monitoring
monitoring.description: Pre-implementation chemical and biological monitoring and historical data were compiled as the project baseline.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Prior to BMP installation, pre-implementation chemical and biological monitoring have been compiled to serve as a baseline for the project along with any historical data available in the Yazoo Pass Watershed (which contains Moon Lake).

monitoring.name: Sonde, benthic macroinvertebrate and chlorophyll-a monitoring
monitoring.description: Historical monitoring included continuous sonde deployment, benthic macroinvertebrate sampling in streams and algal chlorophyll-a in lakes for trophic index determination.
monitoring.parameter: Continuous in-situ data, benthic macroinvertebrates, chlorophyll-a
monitoring.location: Yazoo Pass Watershed streams and Moon Lake
monitoring.sourceQuote: datalogger (sonde) deployment for continuous insitu field measurement data as well as biological community monitoring for benthic macroinvertebrates in streams and algal chlorophyll-a in lakes for trophic index determination.

monitoring.name: Station A0270015 (Yazoo Pass)
monitoring.description: Historical monitoring station on Yazoo Pass sampled in 2009 and 2013 by USGS and MDEQ under the Delta BISQ project.

monitoring.name: Station YZ291 (Moon Lake)
monitoring.description: Historical MDEQ Moon Lake station sampled under nutrient criteria and ambient lakes status and trends programs (2002-2004, 2009, 2011, 2015-2020).
monitoring.parameter: Lake water chemistry and in-situ parameters
monitoring.sourceQuote: YZ291 MDEQ X X

monitoring.name: Station YZ292 (Moon Lake)
monitoring.description: Historical MDEQ Moon Lake station sampled under nutrient criteria and ambient lakes status and trends programs.
monitoring.parameter: Lake water chemistry and in-situ parameters
monitoring.sourceQuote: YZ292 MDEQ X X

monitoring.name: Station YZ431 (Moon Lake)
monitoring.description: Historical MDEQ Moon Lake station sampled under nutrient criteria and ambient lakes status and trends programs.
monitoring.parameter: Lake water chemistry and in-situ parameters
monitoring.sourceQuote: YZ431 MDEQ X X

monitoring.name: Post-implementation monitoring downstream of BMPs
monitoring.description: After BMP installation and stabilization, post-BMP monitoring at locations downstream of BMP activity will be compared with pre-implementation data, possibly over more than one year.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Post-implementation monitoring locations will be selected using best professional judgment and will be targeted to reflect water quality downstream of BMP activity.

monitoring.name: Education program evaluation and attendance
monitoring.description: Evaluation forms, pre/post-tests, surveys and counts of workshop and event attendees will be used to measure the success of education programs.
monitoring.parameter: Number of attendees and knowledge change
monitoring.sourceQuote: Evaluation forms, pre-test/post-test, surveys, and reporting of the number of people who attend workshops, trainings and events are among the methods used to measure the success of education/information programs.

monitoring.name: Final report pollutant reductions and acreage affected
monitoring.description: The grantee's final report will include measured or estimated nonpoint source pollutant reductions, acreage affected and pre- and post-site conditions to track implementation results.
monitoring.parameter: Pollutant load reductions and acreage affected
monitoring.sourceQuote: The grantee shall submit a final report to MDEQ to include measured, or estimated, nonpoint source pollutant reductions or water quality improvements, acreage affected, preand post- site conditions, and GIS data.

outreach.name: Septic system education and outreach materials for lake landowners
outreach.description: MDEQ and the MS Department of Health will give landowners around Moon Lake materials on proper septic system operation and maintenance. This addresses possible pathogen sources in the lake.
outreach.sourceQuote: Along with the MS Department of Health, MDEQ will provide education and outreach materials to landowners around the lake regarding the proper operation and maintenance requirements for septic systems.

outreach.name: Watershed Implementation Team (WIT) face-to-face meetings
outreach.description: The Yazoo Pass WIT stakeholder group will hold at least three face-to-face meetings to share implementation updates and education materials and to review and modify the watershed plan. Project funds will cover food and facility rental.
outreach.sourceQuote: the stakeholder group forming the Yazoo Pass Watershed Implementation Team (WIT) will participate in a minimum of 3 face-to-face meetings.

outreach.name: Meetings with Moon Lake adjacent landowners on bacteria and septic systems
outreach.description: Staff will meet with landowners whose property borders Moon Lake to discuss bacteria in the lake and possible inputs from septic systems.
outreach.audience: landowners with property adjacent to Moon Lake
outreach.sourceQuote: staff will meet with the subset of landowners with property adjacent to Moon Lake to discuss issues related to bacteria in the lake and potential inputs from septic systems.

outreach.name: Teacher Workshops
outreach.description: MDEQ program, listed as usable in this watershed, that trains educators near the watershed about NPS pollution and provides classroom materials.
outreach.sourceQuote: Teacher Workshops – train educators in proximity to the watershed about NPS pollution and provide materials and information that can be used in their classrooms.

outreach.name: Adopt A Stream
outreach.description: Workshops and training for citizens, teachers and students in the Yazoo Pass Watershed, listed among MDEQ programs that could be used in the project.
outreach.sourceQuote: Adopt A Stream - workshops and training venues for citizens, teachers, and students in the Yazoo Pass Watershed.

outreach.name: Water Model Presentations
outreach.description: Enviroscape and groundwater aquifer model presentations with interactive lesson plans, listed as an MDEQ program that could be used in the Yazoo Pass watershed.
outreach.sourceQuote: Water Model Presentations - Enviroscapes and groundwater aquifer models distributed statewide with training and related interactive lesson plans.

outreach.name: Watershed Harmony Mobile Classroom
outreach.description: Mobile classroom program for kindergarten through adults, tailored to 4th and 5th graders, listed as an MDEQ program that could be used in the watershed.
outreach.audience: kindergarten to adults; 4th and 5th grade students
outreach.sourceQuote: Watershed Harmony Mobile Classroom - for ages kindergarten – adults with state and federal public education objectives tailored for 4th and 5th grade students.

outreach.name: Train the Trainer
outreach.description: Workshops and materials for Soil and Water districts, the Extension Service and similar groups, listed as an MDEQ program that could be used in the watershed.
outreach.audience: Soil and Water districts, Extension Service
outreach.sourceQuote: Train the Trainer - workshops and materials for Soil and Water districts, Extension Service, etc.

outreach.name: Waste Pesticide Disposal Event
outreach.description: Event helping farmers and property owners dispose of waste pesticides safely, listed as an MDEQ program that could be used in the watershed.
outreach.sourceQuote: Waste Pesticide Disposal Event - The primary goal of this program is to help Mississippi farmers and property owners minimize the environmental risks associated with the disposal of waste-pesticide products

outreach.name: Inform priority-area landowners and operators about the project
outreach.description: The grantee will inform landowners and operators in priority areas about the project and seek their commitment to participate.
outreach.audience: landowners and operators in priority areas
outreach.sourceQuote: The grantee shall inform landowners and operators within the identified priority areas about the project and secure commitments from these priority-area landowners and operators who are willing to participate in the project. (Months 1-12)

outreach.name: Project presentations as requested by MDEQ
outreach.description: The grantee will give presentations on the project when MDEQ requests them during the project period.
outreach.sourceQuote: The grantee shall make project presentations as requested by MDEQ. (Month 1-36)

outreach.name: Finalize education and outreach plan and schedule events
outreach.description: Milestone to finalize the watershed's education and outreach plan, with outreach events scheduled as the outcome.
outreach.sourceQuote: Finalize education and outreach plan | Education/Outreach events scheduled | Months 8-36

geographicAreas.name: Yazoo Pass Watershed
geographicAreas.description: The 12-digit HUC watershed this 9 Key Element plan covers. It lies mostly in Coahoma County and contains Moon Lake.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Yazoo Pass Watershed (080302040903) is located predominately in northeastern Coahoma County with a small amount in northwestern Quitman County. Yazoo Pass Watershed is a 25,662-acre watershed
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: Element a: Identification of Causes and Sources of Impairment

geographicAreas.name: Coahoma County
geographicAreas.description: The county containing most of the Yazoo Pass Watershed, in its northeastern part.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: located predominately in northeastern Coahoma County with a small amount in northwestern Quitman County
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: Element a: Identification of Causes and Sources of Impairment

geographicAreas.name: Quitman County
geographicAreas.description: The county containing a small part of the Yazoo Pass Watershed, in its northwestern part.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: located predominately in northeastern Coahoma County with a small amount in northwestern Quitman County
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: Element a: Identification of Causes and Sources of Impairment

geographicAreas.name: Moon Lake
geographicAreas.description: The recreational lake in the Yazoo Pass watershed. It is 303(d)-listed (MS320MLM) for sediment and fecal coliform and is the target of the TMDLs and BMP work.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The surface area of Moon Lake is approximately 2,308 acres, and the mean depth is 5.5 meters (FTN, 1991).
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: Element a: Identification of Causes and Sources of Impairment

geographicAreas.name: Phillips Bayou
geographicAreas.description: The bayou that supplies inflow to Moon Lake from the north.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Inflow to Moon Lake enters from Phillips Bayou to the north.
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: Element a: Identification of Causes and Sources of Impairment

geographicAreas.name: Yazoo Pass
geographicAreas.description: The outlet channel through which Moon Lake drains to the east. It is also a monitored water body (station A0270015).
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Moon Lake drains through the Yazoo Pass to the east.
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: Element a: Identification of Causes and Sources of Impairment

geographicAreas.name: Phillips Bayou-Yazoo Pass HUC 10 watershed
geographicAreas.description: The larger 10-digit HUC watershed of which the Yazoo Pass Watershed is a sub-watershed.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Yazoo Pass Watershed is a sub-watershed of the Phillips Bayou-Yazoo Pass larger HUC 10 watershed and is the watershed that contains Moon Lake.
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: Element a: Identification of Causes and Sources of Impairment

geographicAreas.name: Coldwater River (HUC 8) Watershed
geographicAreas.description: The 8-digit HUC basin that includes Moon Lake. Earlier YMD and Delta F.A.R.M. watershed planning and conservation work were carried out at this scale.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Beginning in 1998, the Yazoo-Mississippi Delta Water Management District (YMD) began to organize watershed level meetings throughout the Coldwater River Watershed, which included Moon Lake.
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: Element a: Identification of Causes and Sources of Impairment

geographicAreas.name: Moon Lake Watershed (TMDL area)
geographicAreas.description: The watershed area covered by the 2003 Moon Lake sediment TMDL. It has since been divided into three 12-digit HUCs, one of which is Yazoo Pass.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: the watershed area included in the TMDL has now been divided into three 12-digit HUCs (Figure 2). The lake itself lies in the Yazoo Pass sub- watershed (HUC 080302040903).
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: Element a: Identification of Causes and Sources of Impairment

document.title: Yazoo Pass Watershed 9 Key Element Plan
